end.summary:
Practised predicting and testing whether everyday objects float or sink.
Explored how a hollow bowl shape pushes aside water and can float.
Yash first said steel and clay would always sink, whatever the shape.
They later explained that a hollow bowl shape keeps water out and helps it float; this belief was not fully corrected.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Yash practised making float-or-sink predictions and explaining why a hollow bowl can float while a solid spoon sinks. They gave several correct predictions and later connected the bowl’s hollow shape with keeping water out, but still mixed up the idea that steel or clay must always sink. At home, try floating a clay ball and then reshaping it into a hollow bowl, and ask Yash to predict and explain each result.
